text:
pagerduty: ALERT - pg:connection_pool_high (service: postgres-prod) -> triggered by rule pg.connections > 0.85
incident-bot: Automatic page fired to on-call rota (eng-oncall). Severity: P1.

jordan: acked via PagerDuty :thumbsup:

jordan: I'm on it. seeing a spike in active connections on primary-db-1 (90%).

mira: confirmed, Pg active_connections jumping from ~200 to 950 in last 3m.  max_connections is 1000 but pool queueing/KV cache load causing io_waits.

sara: traffic spike correlated to a canary from app-v2 in us-west-2 — lots of short-lived connections (bursting new connection per request). looks like keepalive not enabled on the client.

jordan: timeline summary — around 09:12 UTC canary rollout started, at 09:17 error rate increased, by 09:19 PagerDuty fired. Affected customers: subset of low-latency API calls routed to us-west-2 (5% of traffic) -> ~5000 requests/min. 3% 5xxs observed.

ops-lead: @jordan @mira do we have automatic fallback to pgbouncer? If not, can we flip a feature flag to reduce connection churn?

jordan: pgbouncer is deployed on app tier but not enabled for this service due to connection pinning. quick mitigation plan: 1) Temporarily disable canary rollout (stop app-v2) 2) Throttle new sessions at ingress LB 3) Increase pg.max_connections by 200 as short-term buffer 4) Reconfigure app clients to reuse connections / enable keepalive and re-run canary with connection pooling.

dmitri: I'm putting an ingress rate limit for the canary hosts now (nginx update). patch: `kubectl patch --type=merge deployment canary-app -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"traffic-control":"throttle-100rps"}}}}}'`

incident-bot: ingress rule applied to canary-app (throttle=100rps). Observed ingress QPS dropping from 1200 -> ~180 over 30s.

mira: applying `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '1200'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();` on primary-db-1 to give breathing room. Doing as a temporary emergency change.

sara: rolling back the canary via CI job: `ci rollback canary-app us-west-2` — job started.

pagerduty: note: Jordan acknowledged and is the assigned responder. Escalation policy will escalate to ops-lead in 8m if not resolved.

jordan: checking replication lag and read-replica capacity to offload some queries. read-replica r-2 currently at lag <50ms, can take some read traffic.

mira: enabling application read routing for safe routes (feature flag `route_reads_to_replicas=true`) on the API gateway for non-transactional endpoints.

jordan: after ingress throttle + canary rollback + pg max_connections bump — active connections dropping: 950 -> 420 in 2m. 5xx rate reduced to 0.7%. latency back down to baseline for most customers but US-west still seeing elevated p50 by ~40ms for a subset of requests.

ops-lead: good. @sara can you coordinate a customer-facing note for the account managers? minimal impact but some customers saw transient 5xxs between 09:17-09:25 UTC.

sara: on it. Drafted quick blurb: "We experienced a brief increase in database connections during a canary deployment which caused transient errors for a subset of API calls in us-west-2 between 09:17-09:25 UTC. The canary has been rolled back and normal service restored. We're following up with improvements to connection pooling and rollout practices." Will send in 2 mins.

dmitri: monitoring for secondary effects — Redis lookups also spiked due to retry traffic. eviction rate up but not critical. px: `redis-cluster evicted_keys/sec` hit 120 -> now down to 15.

mira: creating a post-incident TODO: 1) Enforce connection pooling on client SDK 2) Add pre-deploy check for connection churn during canary 3) Enable pgbouncer for this service 4) Autoscale read-replicas for short spikes 5) Add circuit-breaker on clients to avoid full fanout retries.

jordan: handoff to postmortem owner: @mira — please own postmortem. I'll leave notes and logs in the incident channel.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by jordan at 09:22 UTC. Incident resolved -> resolved at 09:27 UTC (root cause mitigated, temporary config changes applied).

ops-lead: thanks everyone. quick checklist before closing: verify all emergency config changes reverted or made safe as permanent if reviewed.

jordan: will revert `max_connections` bump after traffic normalizes — setting a reminder: `at now + 30 minutes` to `ALTER SYSTEM SET max_connections = '1000'; SELECT pg_reload_conf();`

mira: created postmortem draft: https://redwood.internal/docs/incidents/2479993331 (placeholder). Will include timeline, metrics, and remediation PRs.

sara: customer note posted and sent to accounts.

dmitri: monitoring continues, no regressions seen in last 10m.

jordan: closing thread here — will update postmortem and link follow-ups. great quick work team :heart:

(reacts: :thumbsup: from ops-lead, :clap: from sara)
